message.text: Found the key files. Now examining webhook.go and validate.go to identify the outbound delivery function and its protection against internal network addresses.

The outbound HTTP delivery executes in `webhook.Post()` within `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

The actual HTTP call runs at line 152 via `safeClient.Do(req)` inside `Post()`. The protection mechanism is `ValidateURL` in `validate.go`, which rejects URLs resolving to private or reserved IP addresses during webhook registration.

The primary runtime protection is `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go`, which blocks dial attempts to reserved or private IPs via a custom Transport on `safeClient`. This uses `isReservedIP` from valigo. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` also rejects URLs resolving to reserved or private addresses during webhook registration.
Checking where ValidateURL is called in user_service_webhooks.go.

The outbound delivery executes in the `Post` function within `internal/webhook/webhook.go`, called by async workers after `PostAsync` enqueues the request.

`safeDialContext` on the `safeClient` HTTP transport blocks reserved and private IPs at dial time. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` rejects URLs that resolve to internal addresses during registration.

The shared `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` logic lives in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. `safeDialContext` is defined in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

`safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` is the delivery-time protection. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` guards registration, though legacy webhooks or direct database edits could bypass it.

The answer will list `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. This avoids redundancy, since `safeDialContext` is the delivery-time guard and `isReservedIP` is shared via `validate.go`.
